Confidence Interval for the Difference of Two Medians

Source: R/medianDiffCI.R
medianDiffCI.Rd

Calculates the confidence interval for the difference of two medians, median(x) - median(y), either with the distribution-free method of Bonett and Price or with the bootstrap.

Usage

medianDiffCI(
  x,
  y,
  conf.level = 0.95,
  sides = c("two.sided", "left", "right"),
  method = c("bonett-price", "boot"),
  paired = FALSE,
  na.rm = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

a (non-empty) numeric vector of data values.

y

a (non-empty) numeric vector of data values.

conf.level

confidence level of the interval.

sides

a character string specifying the side of the confidence interval, must be one of "two.sided" (default), "left" or "right". You can specify just the initial letter. "left" would be analogue to a hypothesis of "greater" in a t.test.

method

a character string, either "bonett-price" (default) or "boot". The bootstrap type can be provided by the dots, see boot::boot.ci().

paired

a logical indicating whether x and y are paired. Defaults to FALSE. Requires method = "boot".

na.rm

logical. Should missing values be removed? Defaults to FALSE. For paired data, incomplete pairs are removed.

...

further arguments passed to the bootstrap, e.g. R and type.

Value

A named numeric vector with elements:

mediandiff

point estimate, the difference median(x) - median(y)

lci

lower confidence interval bound

uci

upper confidence interval bound

Details

method = "bonett-price" (default) estimates the standard error of each sample median from a pair of order statistics, $$\widehat{se}_j = \frac{Y_{(n_j - c_j + 1)} - Y_{(c_j)}}{2 z_j}, \quad c_j = \mathrm{round}\left(\frac{n_j}{2} - \sqrt{n_j}\right),$$ where \(z_j\) is the normal quantile matching the exact binomial coverage of \([Y_{(c_j)}, Y_{(n_j - c_j + 1)}]\), and combines both into a normal interval. No distributional assumption is made, and the variances of the two groups may differ. It is available for independent samples only.

method = "boot" resamples within each group (stratified), or whole pairs if paired = TRUE. The bootstrap distribution of a median is discrete and lumpy in small samples; type = "perc" is the robust choice there. The bootstrap type "stud" is not supported, as the statistic returns no per-replicate variance estimate.

Note that for paired data the difference of the medians is not the median of the differences. For the latter, use medianCI(x - y). Neither is it the Hodges-Lehmann shift estimate reported by wilcox.test(), which coincides with the median difference only under a pure location shift.

References

Bonett, D. G. and Price, R. M. (2002). Statistical inference for a linear function of medians: confidence intervals, hypothesis testing, and sample size requirements. Psychological Methods 7(3), 370–383. doi:10.1037//1082-989x.7.3.370

Price, R. M. and Bonett, D. G. (2002). Distribution-free confidence intervals for difference and ratio of medians. Journal of Statistical Computation and Simulation 72(2), 119–124. doi:10.1080/00949650212140

See also

meanDiffCI(), medianCI(), boot::boot.ci()

Other ci.location: meanCI(), meanCIn(), meanDiffCI(), medianCI(), quantileCI(), sumCI()

Examples

x <- mtcars[mtcars$am == 0, "mpg"]
y <- mtcars[mtcars$am == 1, "mpg"]

medianDiffCI(x, y)
#>  mediandiff         lci         uci 
#>  -5.5000000 -10.4651329  -0.5348671 
medianDiffCI(x, y, conf.level = 0.99)
#> mediandiff        lci        uci 
#>  -5.500000 -12.025291   1.025291 
medianDiffCI(x, y, sides = "left")
#> mediandiff        lci        uci 
#>  -5.500000  -9.666871        Inf 

# bootstrap
set.seed(1)
medianDiffCI(x, y, method = "boot", type = "perc")
#> mediandiff        lci        uci 
#>       -5.5      -14.0       -2.2 
medianDiffCI(x, y, method = "boot", type = "bca")
#> mediandiff        lci        uci 
#>       -5.5      -12.6       -1.8 

# paired: difference of medians vs. median of differences
set.seed(2)
drug2 <- sleep$extra[sleep$group == 2]
drug1 <- sleep$extra[sleep$group == 1]
medianDiffCI(drug2, drug1, method = "boot", paired = TRUE, type = "perc")
#> mediandiff        lci        uci 
#>       1.40       0.75       3.70 
medianCI(drug2 - drug1)
#> median    lci    uci 
#>    1.3    0.8    2.4 
#> attr(,"conf.level")
#> [1] 0.9785156
